facts.statement: Malawisuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian mesoeucrocodylian found in the Early Cretaceous Dinosaur Beds of Malawi.
facts.quote: Malawisuchus (meaning "Malawi crocodile") is an extinct genus of notosuchian mesoeucrocodylian from the Early Cretaceous Dinosaur Beds of Malawi.

facts.statement: Elizabeth Gomani formally described Malawisuchus in 1997 as a member of the family Notosuchidae.
facts.quote: Malawisuchus was described in 1997 by Elizabeth Gomani as a member of the family Notosuchidae.

facts.statement: The type species M. mwakasyungutiensis is named after Mwakasyunguti, the area in northern Malawi where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The type species is M. mwakasyungutiensis, referring to Mwakasyunguti, the area of northern Malawi where it was found.

facts.statement: Carvalho and colleagues reclassified Malawisuchus as a member of the family Itasuchidae in 2004.
facts.quote: It was classified as a member of the family Itasuchidae by Carvalho and colleagues in 2004.

facts.statement: Malawisuchus possessed unusual, mammal-like teeth, including those with multiple cusps at the rear of the jaw.
facts.quote: It had unusual, mammal-like teeth, including teeth with multiple cusps in the rear of the jaw.

facts.statement: The jaw joint of Malawisuchus suggests it processed food using a forward motion.
facts.quote: Its jaw joint suggests it processed food with a forward motion.

facts.statement: Malawisuchus had a strong neck, hind legs suggesting an upright posture and ability to run, and upper arm muscles indicating it could dig.
facts.quote: The neck was strong, and the articulations of the hind leg suggest an upright posture and an ability to run, while the muscle attachments on the upper arm suggest digging

facts.statement: The preservation of articulated specimens suggests Malawisuchus lived in or was preserved within burrows.
facts.quote: additionally, the taphonomy of articulated specimens suggests that they had been preserved in burrows.

facts.statement: Malawisuchus was a small crocodilian reaching a length of about 60 centimetres (24 inches).
facts.quote: It was a small crocodilian, only about 60 centimetres long (24 in).

facts.statement: Malawisuchus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Malawisuchus as Candidodontidae.

rejected.statement: Malawisuchus was first discovered in 1989 but remained undescribed until 1997.
rejected.quote: Malawisuchus was first discovered in 1989, but not formally described for several years.
